subject: Post-demo: model prioritization, benchmarks, and next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@finlytics.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: model prioritization, benchmarks, and next steps

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and our recommended next steps based on the demo and the Finlytics priorities you highlighted (low tail latency, conservative hallucination risk, and throughput for batch enrichment jobs). I attached the prompt set we used and the XLSX with raw bench runs.

IDEA: run a targeted 1-week pilot across three candidate model configurations, prioritized by risk/cost tradeoff. Shortlist with quick rationale below (estimates are for hosted US-west; per-1k-token cost and p95 latency shown):

1) redwood-s-8b-q8 (low-cost, low-latency)
   - Cost: ~$0.60 / 1k tokens
   - p95 latency: ~120ms per token (interactive flows); init latency ~180ms
   - Quality: good for template-driven extraction and summary tasks; occasional factual lapses on long-chain reasoning
   - Why try: meets your interactive SLAs and is cheapest for high throughput enrichment. Recommend for customer-facing UI where latency matters most.

2) redwood-m-13b-q4 (balanced quality/latency)
   - Cost: ~$1.90 / 1k tokens
   - p95 latency: ~220ms per token
   - Quality: noticeably better on instruction-following and fewer hallucinations on knowledge lookups
   - Why try: best middle-ground for mixed workloads — lower jitter than the 70B but higher quality than 8B. Good candidate for summary + fact-check stage.

3) gptx-70b-fp16 (high-quality fallback)
   - Cost: ~$8.40 / 1k tokens (hosted high-tier)
   - p95 latency: ~420ms per token (higher variability)
   - Quality: strongest factuality on long documents and multi-step reasoning; helpful for edge-case escalations
   - Why try: use as a fallback for high-risk documents or nightly re-run where accuracy > cost.

Proposed pilot plan (concrete):
- Week 0: load Finlytics prompt set (attached) + anonymized sample corpus (you provide).
- Week 1: run 2 x 1k-sample evaluations per model (A/B), collect latency, ROUGE/F1 on labeled set, hallucination count, and token-cost estimates.
- Week 2: measure production-like 95th percentile tail latency with bursty traffic pattern; enable KV caching and compare cost delta.

Next steps I recommend we take this week:
- You: share a 5–10K anonymized sample (or subset) for the evaluation run.
- Us: schedule a 45-minute pilot kickoff (I can run through evaluation plan + benchmarks).
- Internal: I’ll loop in Marissa for the regression monitoring plan and Vanessa for pilot pricing.

Attachments: Finlytics-eval-promptset-v1.jsonl, benchmarks-20270406.xlsx, pilot-MAP-sow-draft.pdf

Open questions we flagged on the demo: any regulatory constraints requiring on-prem deployment? (You mentioned SOC 2 earlier) and approx. monthly token volume for enrichment vs UI usage.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with proposed times for a kickoff.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 08 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model prioritization, benchmarks, and next steps

Karthik — thanks for the clear recap. This aligns with what we discussed. A few quick points/questions: 

- Priority: low tail latency for the web UI (sub-250ms target) and low hallucination for final reports — accuracy there matters more than cost.
- We can provide a 7k anonymized sample corpus by EOD Friday. I will strip PII.
- Can you include a short example output (2–3 examples) from each model on our prompt set so our stakeholders can eyeball hallucination differences?
- We will likely need an NDA addendum for some of the sample data. I’ll loop legal if needed.

Also curious on how caching interacts with the UI flow you recommended — does prefix/KV caching reduce p95 materially for the 13B?

If you can send the sample outputs + a proposed kickoff time, I’ll confirm with the team.

— Sarah
Sarah Jenkins | Head of Data Products | Finlytics
email: sarah.jenkins@finlytics.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 08 Apr 2027 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model prioritization, benchmarks, and next steps

Adding a few operational items for the evaluation so we capture regressions early: 

- Metric definitions: ROUGE-L (summary fidelity), Exact-match slices for key entities, and a hallucination flag (binary) judged by the labeled subset.
- Regression alert: set a baseline per-model on day-0 results and trigger an alert if hallucination rate increases >5% or ROUGE-L drops >3 pts during the pilot.
- Eval plan: run 1,000 paired prompts per model (A/B) across both the UI prompt set and enrichment batch set. We'll also run a small adversarial prompt subset (50 samples) to stress-test hallucination.
- Caching: enable KV caching and compare a run with cache-on vs cache-off. Expect ~15–25% token-cost savings for repeated prefix patterns; p95 can improve by ~30–40% in some UI flows. Document these in the benchmark spreadsheet.

I’ll prepare a lightweight QA template for reviewers and a short rubric so your stakeholders can grade hallucination severity consistently.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole | Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: model prioritization, benchmarks, and next steps

Thanks all — quick commercial note: based on the projected consumption you gave (ballpark yesterday), we can include a 3-month pilot on Dedicated Reserved capacity with a capped monthly commit to keep unit costs predictable. I’ll draft two options:

A) Hosted pilot (no long-term commit): faster to start, per-token pricing as Karthik outlined.
B) Dedicated 3-month pilot: lower variable unit cost once committed; includes basic SLA and audit logging (useful if Finlytics brings sensitive data).

I’ll attach short pricing bullets in the kickoff invite. For now, Sarah — if you expect regulated docs, Dedicated may simplify compliance.

— Vanessa
